name: Samuel Drew
life: “I still remember a gig where I played as the curtain fell.” Monday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Samuel stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I walked away because my wrists hurt. I want the new drummer to know that was a choice, too.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cream pullover and a thin silver ring worn on a cord. Samuel has a straight nose and deep-set eyes, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Samuel draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting during a conversation.
personality: Samuel finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To explain the choice to stop drumming to the replacement.
family: Julius Mitchell is Samuel’s stepsibling. The eldest person in the family used to sign cards with a large unsteady X. Everyone took this as a flourish until she asked someone to teach her the rest of her name. Samuel checks whether there is a way to sign or answer in private. Asked about *The hair after illness*, Julius says, “I print portrait cards. I offered one photograph from behind so she could look before sharing it.”
connections: Riley Fox (regular substitute). The original drummer promises the overlooked substitute a private rehearsal.

reactions.situation: The drummer asks the substitute to keep the stool
reactions.response: Samuel asks whether the drummer means a loan or a gift.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Samuel asks them privately what can be shared about the delay and respects the answer.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Samuel waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
